summary: This section explains how existing companies get officially registered under the new law. Once the company follows all the registration rules and pays the required fees, the Registrar issues a signed certificate. This certificate proves the company is now officially registered under this Act.
points: The company must follow the registration rules given in this chapter.
The company must pay any fees required under section 403.
The Registrar will provide a signed certificate of incorporation.
The certificate will state if the company is a limited company.
The company becomes officially incorporated once these steps are complete.
example: Apex Traders, an older business, wants to become a registered company under the new Companies Act, 2013. The managers carefully complete all the necessary registration steps outlined in the chapter. They also pay the official fees as required by section 403. After checking everything, the Registrar signs and issues a certificate confirming that Apex Traders is now incorporated under the Act. For a limited company, the certificate also clearly states that it is limited. From that moment on, Apex Traders is officially recognized as a company under the new law.

terms.meaning: The government official who keeps records of companies and handles their registration.
Officially formed and recognized as a legal company.
A company where the financial liability of the owners is restricted.

watch: Make sure to remember that this section only applies after all registration rules and fee payments are fully completed.
